correction: Version 1 of this file concluded that value-indexed dispatch was blocked. That conclusion was wrong. The trace shows the real mechanism: `MOVD X` moves D to the operand and the following Jmp jumps to the address contained in that operand cell. Cell content selects the next code block. The table-at-low-addresses failure is real but narrower: it blocks one specific table layout, not dispatch itself.

sequence: step=1801 c=1898 jmp -> c = mem[d] (d=59032, ENTRY) -> MOVD code block
step=1802 c=2034 movd -> d = mem[d] (the operand word) + increment
step=1803 c=2035 jmp -> c = mem[d] = content of DISPATCH -> ROT code block
the trailing Jmp of each code block consumes the next data word as the next target
mechanism.statement: The data section is a threaded program: each data word holds (target-1). A Jmp reads the current word's content as the next C. Jumping into the data section at a chosen word executes whatever block that word references.
mechanism.corollary: Value-indexed dispatch = make the operand word's CONTENT depend on the runtime value. Binary dispatch on a cycle cell (Nop vs MovD) is the native form; the adder and the counter use it. Full tables need either low addresses (blocked by generated init code) or indexed address arithmetic (not available).

positive.jumpchain.hell: DISPATCH contains a ROT code reference; the chain ROT('A'<<1), OUT, HALT prints 'A'. Steps 1801-1808.
positive.dispatch_HALT.hell: DISPATCH contains HALT; the program halts immediately with no output.
positive.note: Changing the CONTENT of the dispatch word changes which code block runs: this is the dispatch primitive.

negative_narrow.claim: A handler TABLE at addresses ~v (low range) is impossible in LMAO: its generated initialization code occupies the low addresses and overlap is rejected in normal and -f mode.

claim: LMAO_DISPATCH_MECHANISM=DEMONSTRATED (content-of-cell selects next code block). LMAO_LOW_ADDRESS_TABLE=NOT_DEMONSTRATED (narrow, layout-specific).
